title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users (Part II)
gist: OpenAI describes how its Habitat storage platform on Azure Cosmos DB scaled to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users and 500+ PB, cycling from shared to isolated to shared multi-tenancy, cutting global read p50 from about 120 ms to 10 ms, and now building an in-house exabyte-scale store.

insights.claim: OpenAI's Habitat storage platform serves over 1 billion users across 40 geographic regions and holds over 500 petabytes of data.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete measure of ChatGPT's data-infrastructure footprint, a demand signal for cloud storage and databases.

insights.claim: OpenAI's largest Azure Cosmos DB account stores tens of petabytes and serves more than 20M QPS, which OpenAI believes makes it the only company running Cosmos DB at that scale.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Shows Azure's flagship database being stress-tested by OpenAI; scale reference for Microsoft's AI-driven cloud demand.
insights.quote: To our knowledge, we are the only company which has deployed Azure Cosmos DB at this scale.

insights.claim: OpenAI went from one shared Cosmos DB container to per-use-case single-tenant containers and back to a shared multi-tenant container, because dedicated containers made nearly every product team responsible for capacity planning and launches routinely hit last-minute scaling incidents.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Single-tenancy isolation costs organisational overhead that scales badly; shared systems with QoS win at hyperscale.

insights.claim: Dedicated containers lose the workload-mixing benefit of shared systems: a launch going from 1K to 1M RU/s is 5% of headroom on a 100M RU/s shared container but 10,000% on a 10K RU/s dedicated one.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Illustrates why aggregate smoothing makes shared capacity cheaper and safer for spiky AI product launches.
insights.locator: Figure 03 · Lack of stable aggregate growth

insights.claim: Partition splits shrink per-partition throughput because provisioned container throughput stays fixed while physical partitions multiply, so storage growth alone can starve active workloads at stable request rates.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: A hidden failure mode for storage-heavy, blob-like workloads on provisioned-throughput databases.
insights.quote: The result is that the effective throughput limit per partition shrinks as data size grows.

insights.claim: After adopting hot-key throttling, request-tier QoS and a custom serverless mode built by the Azure team, OpenAI moved back to one shared container and reports no provisioning or noisy-neighbor incidents in the months since.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Evidence of deep OpenAI-Microsoft co-engineering; Azure ships product features tailored to OpenAI's scale.

insights.claim: OpenAI argues that at its scale managed cloud services become less managed and require shared tests, dashboards, direct engineer-to-engineer paging and joint ownership of failure modes with the provider.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Frontier AI labs are effectively co-developing cloud infrastructure with hyperscalers, deepening vendor lock-in and partnership.
insights.quote: At scale, managed services become less managed and require deep integrations with the service provider at all levels from design to operations.

insights.claim: Two outages in late 2024, a regional power failure whose failover took hours and a failback connection stampede that overwhelmed the Cosmos DB gateway, exposed untested failover at OpenAI's scale.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Concentration risk: a single regional database event can hit ChatGPT availability.

insights.claim: Habitat's global read p50 latency fell from roughly 120 ms to roughly 10 ms, a 12x improvement, from replicating critical data nearby, launching in-region caching, and a Rust rewrite of the service.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Latency-driven product quality gains come from infrastructure engineering, not just model improvements.

insights.claim: Reads make up over 90% of Habitat requests, and Habitat uses Valkey lookaside caches invalidated via the Cosmos DB change feed, following Meta's TAO, to propagate invalidations globally within seconds.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: CDC-driven cache invalidation is the pattern for read-heavy global AI apps; relevant to Valkey/Redis-compatible caching demand.
insights.locator: Rely on integrated caching for everything else

insights.claim: Data placement near users is often blocked by physical cloud capacity, so in regions with limited datacenter power, cooling or capacity OpenAI must choose between local storage and extra serving compute.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Power and cooling constraints are binding on AI infrastructure placement even for storage, reinforcing the datacenter-capacity bottleneck thesis.
insights.locator: Store data near users when capacity allows

insights.claim: Replicating only the smallest, latency-critical datasets, such as authentication metadata, to all 40 Azure regions is possible but capacity-constrained and limited to a few hand-selected datasets.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Global replication cost caps how much data can be kept hot everywhere.
insights.locator: Broadly replicate only the smallest and most latency-sensitive datasets

insights.claim: OpenAI is building an in-house exabyte-scale online storage system combining Rockset's RocksDB Cloud core with Raft replication, using disaggregated storage and physical replication to cut flash needs in exchange for lower peak QPS.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Signals potential long-term in-sourcing of core storage from Azure; watch flash demand and cloud-database share.
insights.quote: custom in-house exabyte-scale online storage system

insights.claim: OpenAI's change-data-capture platform handles millions of captured changes per second across thousands of containers through more than a hundred Kafka topics, powering secondary indexes, data movement and analytics.
insights.speaker: OpenAI Blog
insights.so_what: Scale reference for streaming-infrastructure demand such as Kafka.
